course_name_original: Materiales y tecnologías en fabricación mecánica
course_name_en: Materials and Technologies in Mechanical Manufacturing
prerequisites: Fundamentals of Manufacturing Systems and Technologies
To enroll in this course, it is necessary to have passed or to be enrolled in all courses from years prior to the year in which this course is located.

learning_outcomes.text: Know the technological basis supporting the most recent research in the use of machine tools and equipment for forming manufacturing and coordinate measuring machines.
Know the main materials used in machine components.
Know the requirements of different components for an adequate selection of materials.
Know the experimental process used when working with high-speed machines (HSM) for machining manufacturing.
learning_outcomes.code: B4 B5 B6 B8 C26 D5 D7 D8 D9 D10

learning_outcomes.text: Know current technologies for improving surface properties: wear and corrosion resistance. Acquire criteria for selecting the most appropriate surface treatment to extend a component's service life.
Apply Fracture Mechanics criteria in machinery design.

Identify and interpret possible causes of material failures based on service conditions. Propose solutions to prevent component failure. Acquire skills for performing and interpreting non-destructive tests.
Analyze and propose operational solutions to problems in the field of materials engineering.
learning_outcomes.code: B4 B5 B7 C25 D5 D7 D8 D9 D14

learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrates communication and teamwork skills. Identifies own information needs and uses available resources, spaces, and services to design and execute searches appropriate to the thematic area.
Carries out assigned tasks based on basic guidance from the professor, deciding the duration of the parts, including personal contributions, and expanding information sources.
learning_outcomes.code: B4 B6 D5 D7 D8 D10

learning_outcomes.text: Deepen knowledge of machine tool verification techniques.

learning_outcomes.code: B4 B5 B6 B8 C26 D5 D8 D9 D10 D14 D17 D20

learning_outcomes.text: Be able to analyze with advanced methods the influence of material processing on the selection and use of forming equipment.
Be able to perform a CAE analysis of forming processes.

syllabus_topics: 1. Materials used in machine elements: types and properties.
1.3 Materials for gears, bearings, and springs.
2.1 Application of fracture mechanics to design.
4.1 Wear. Evaluation tests and strategies for improving wear resistance.
4.2 Corrosion. Anti-corrosion protection technology. Analysis of practical cases.
2.1. Study of the influence of material processing on the in-service behavior of machinery and equipment for mechanical manufacturing by
2.2. Study of Machinery Resources: Machine-Tools, Presses, and other equipment for mechanical manufacturing and dimensional control
2.2.2. Verification, adjustment, and tuning: Rigidity evaluation, Acceleration measurement.
2.2.4. Real-time use and control. Modeling and characterization.
teaching_methods: Lecture: Basic content exposition. Resolution of exercises, problems, and cases. Evaluation of the learning process through objective tests.
Seminar: Resolution of practical cases. Tutoring of works and monitoring of the learning process.
Laboratory practices: Conducting tests and applying specific techniques in the laboratory. Resolution of cases. Use of software combined with experiences in the manufacturing workshop.
Presentation: Oral presentation of individual and group tutored work.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance, participation, and reports for practical activities
Memoirs and/or projects for practical activities

assessment_rules: Students can choose between two evaluation systems: A (final exam only) or B (continuous evaluation). For System B (continuous evaluation), the final grade consists of written tests (50% of the total: 20% from a mid-term test and 30% from the final exam) and practical activities (50% of the total: 20% from attendance, participation, and reports, and 30% from memoirs and/or projects). To pass the course under either system, students must obtain a minimum of 40% in each of the two thematic blocks (Materials and Technologies) and a final grade of at least 50%. If the 40% minimum in each block is not met, the final grade will be capped at 4.9. The second and third call (resit) will only use System A (final exam only).
